DeForest Abogados advises domestic and multinational employers on labour advisory, litigation, collective labour relations, social security, compliance and workforce governance matters throughout Mexico. Its work covers the employment lifecycle, including hiring and day-to-day advice, collective bargaining, restructurings, regulatory inspections, social security issues and employment litigation.

The practice acts for companies in regulated and labour-intensive sectors, including automotive, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, retail, technology, telecommunications and financial services. It advises on collective bargaining and union representation matters, labour integration following M&A transactions, employer restructurings, labour and social security audits, constitutional proceedings, preventive compliance programmes and inspections before the Ministry of Labour, IMSS and INFONAVIT.

The firm advises employers with a combined workforce exceeding one million employees in Mexico. Its contentious work includes nationwide litigation portfolios comprising hundreds of simultaneous proceedings, including approximately 700 labour disputes managed by the Puebla team. The practice has also assisted more than 20 clients in connection with Ministry of Labour inspections and has handled labour and social security compliance audits.

Eduardo Garduño brings more than two decades of experience advising corporations on labour matters, together with public-sector experience. Jaime Bustamante previously served as Legal Director for Mexico, Central America and South America at ManpowerGroup. Raymundo Carreño was General Legal Director of Volkswagen de México for nearly four decades.

Other practitioners include Javier Atzin Vallejo, whose work focuses on labour compliance, social security and workforce integration; Edgar Barreto, who handles labour litigation and IMSS matters; Andrés Cabrera, who leads the firm’s labour practice in the Bajío region; Erick Pérez, whose practice includes litigation and constitutional proceedings; and José Alberto Díaz, who advises on labour, social security and administrative litigation in regulated industries.
